- If sentiment is strongly positive (≥ 0.7) and forecast is flat or rising slowly, reduce forecast slope to avoid over-optimism.  
- If sentiment is negative (≤ -0.5) and forecast is rising, cap upward momentum; model may be ignoring bearish signals.  
- After a sharp price spike, forecast should not immediately continue rising — allow for mean reversion or correction in 3–5 days.  
- When sentiment swings sharply (e.g., from +0.9 to -0.7), model should adjust forecast downward with lagged sensitivity to avoid delayed reaction.  
- If forecast is consistently below true outcome for 3+ consecutive days, check for sentiment lag — model may be underreacting to bullish sentiment.  
- For long-term (30d) forecasts, avoid linear extrapolation — price often reverts to mean or shows asymmetric behavior after volatility spikes.  
- If sentiment is neutral or mixed (±0.3), forecast should not be overly confident — avoid smooth, upward trends unless supported by strong momentum.
